corpus.text: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act provides for liquidated damages where a contract stipulates a sum named as a genuine pre-estimate of loss. The Supreme Court in Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA held that proof of actual loss is essential unless impossible or difficult to prove.

In breach of contract claims under Section 73 and 74, liquidated damages represent an upper ceiling on recoverable compensation rather than an automatic penalty. Penal stipulations and extortionate forfeit clauses are strictly unenforceable.

In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), a nine-judge Constitution Bench held that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right protected under Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution, subject to proportionality and legitimate state aim.

Under the Public Trust Doctrine and the Polluter Pays Principle recognized in Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum, the polluter is liable to pay the costs of remedial action, restoring environmental degradation, and compensating victims of pollution.

metadata.case_name: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. UOI

corpus.text: Under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, an arbitral award can only be set aside if it violates the public policy of India or suffers from patent illegality appearing on the face of the award, without reappreciating evidentiary merits.

The grant of regular bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires satisfaction of the judicial triple test: flight risk, danger of tampering with evidence, and likelihood of influencing witnesses or committing further offences.
